source: the decision record, reworded by Sol for TD-462 and scoped by TD-442 on 2026-10-22; the owner checked the four Sol left uncertain (TD-464)
notes: The nine ECC adoptions (TD-115) stand in the record as their own lines: 1-3 and 6-9 under Standalone (TD-468), 4 in C-26's test curation line, 5 in Standalone's watcher lessons line; all nine are Global (TD-442).
TD-442 does not make every test or memory decision Global, only the ECC ones.
The quality service is split in the record: its config-approval line is Global (TD-442), the line that runs linters is OwlBear's.
Page-comment policy (C-01's exception) and the scope mapping itself stay OwlBear's under “all else”.

A second Sol check (2026-10-22) corrected 8 drifting and 2 still-dependent rewordings and kept 29 originals that already stood alone; the 4 it left uncertain were split or retired with the owner (TD-467 to TD-469).

global.original: A read-back offers three close variants of the decision, fewer only when fewer really differ, never padded, the matching one at varying positions, plus one or two other directions, the opposite among them.
It closes with "take your recommendation (…)" naming it, "none of these: show me more options" and "explain first"; free text stays open; no other recommendation mark.
The question shows the decision's record and what changed since.
When the direction itself is in doubt, ask the direction first, then the nuances, stating the reason.
Used at the end of ideation, before design approval and for the assistant's consequential choices.
"Take your recommendation" makes the result the assistant's `autonomous` choice, with reasons.
"Show me more options" gives a bounded set across directions, each with pros, cons, risks and its own percentage that it is a good choice, not adding up.
For a free-text chat answer, offer 2 to 5 readings that fill gaps differently, plus "your words as written", "show me more readings" and "explain first"; the owner chooses the one meant.
Every challenge of owner input extracts intent and reports what is missing and what is overdone, not only what is wrong; the owner's words are evidence of intent, not a literal spec.
Free text and unclear answers are read back at once; a chosen paraphrase counts as confirmed; a session ends with one check of everything it records.
Every security restriction and every security relaxation the assistant introduces is reviewed with the owner.
Research about a consumer project is never committed into that project.
Keep, rewrite lower, merge or retire; doubt keeps. A removal names the behaviour, a plausible bug and the test that still catches it; security guards, incident regressions and public contracts stay.
Watcher lessons need evidence that agent behaviour caused the signal; merging lessons belongs to the curator.
Agents request changes to lint and format configs, CI workflows and Git hooks and the owner approves; direct agent edits are refused from the start; no existing suppression is grandfathered.
The builder never deletes, skips or weakens a test or check to get green; the reviewer reports any that does.
A defect fix prefers existing tests that tell the bug apart and shows failing-before evidence where feasible; otherwise it states its reproduction basis and gap.
The reviewer checks whether a caller already handles a problem and reports fallbacks that hide failures.
The shaper never infers business constraints from code; criteria may say what must not happen; it asks for the observable pain, the current workaround and evidence against its assumptions.
UI work covers a partial state, pointer target size per WCAG 2.5.8 with its exceptions, and modal focus containment and return, proven in a browser.
The planner finds a change's consumers from real imports and puts their tests in the task's checks.
Builder and reviewer trace state changes in the order they happen.

reworded.original: It closes with "take your recommendation (…)" naming it, "none of these: show me more options" and "explain first"; free text stays open; no other recommendation mark.
reworded.statement: A decision read-back closes with "take your recommendation (...)" naming the recommendation, "none of these: show me more options" and "explain first"; free text stays open; no other recommendation mark.

reworded.original: The question shows the decision's record and what changed since.
reworded.statement: A decision read-back question shows the decision's record and what changed since it was recorded.

reworded.original: Used at the end of ideation, before design approval and for the assistant's consequential choices.
reworded.statement: Use the decision read-back format at the end of ideation, before design approval and for the assistant's consequential choices.

reworded.original: The watcher's model and effort are chosen with the owner after TD-27's benchmark has run.
reworded.statement: Choose the watcher's model and effort with the owner after benchmarking OwlBear work: gpt-6-luna max vs claude-haiku-5.5 high, and claude-haiku-5.5 xhigh vs gpt-6.1-sol low, for quality and cost.
reworded.note: corrected by a second check: Replaces TD-27's two specified model/effort comparisons with an unspecified three-model benchmark.

reworded.original: Accept is offered for a step's own session and a screenshot round; challenge sessions only rerun.
reworded.statement: Accepting a result whose model is unknown is offered for a step's own session and a screenshot round; challenge sessions only rerun.

reworded.topic: C-04 Window steps and the watcher
reworded.original: Before real-project use: New Change, automatic merge with pull-back, thread replies and resolution, visual pre-check, deterministic "now" line, step time, quiet warning, credits and the watcher.
reworded.statement: Before real projects use OwlBear, provide New Change, automatic merge with pull-back, thread replies and resolution, visual pre-check, a deterministic "now" line, step time, quiet warning, credits and the watcher.

reworded.topic: C-04 Window steps and the watcher
reworded.original: Afterwards, watching may change only how writes outside the worktree are controlled; everything else stays the same.
reworded.statement: Once the watcher exists, watching SDK steps may change only how writes outside the worktree are controlled; everything else about the steps stays the same.

reworded.topic: C-04 Window steps and the watcher
reworded.original: The watcher judges each outside write and outgoing transfer after the fact, stopping the step only if dangerous or inappropriate for the task; harmless ones are reported.
reworded.statement: The watcher judges each write outside the worktree and each outgoing data transfer after the fact, stopping the step only if dangerous or inappropriate for the task; harmless ones are reported.

reworded.topic: C-04 Window steps and the watcher
reworded.original: Delivery's own state, temporary files and the user's tool caches are never judged.
reworded.statement: The watcher never judges writes to Delivery's own state, temporary files or the user's tool caches.

reworded.topic: C-04 Window steps and the watcher
reworded.original: The whole watcher is built right after the window-step gate.
reworded.statement: Build the whole watcher immediately after the gate for safely reopening VS Code window steps.

reworded.topic: C-04 Window steps and the watcher
reworded.original: Suspended while window steps are paused, reviewed when the gate passes: runtime and visibility routing, window start, the per-project window switch, the read-only worktree.
reworded.statement: Runtime and visibility routing, window startup, the per-project window-runtime switch and the read-only worktree are suspended while window steps are paused; review them when the window-step reopening gate passes.

reworded.topic: C-04 Window steps and the watcher
reworded.original: Suspended routing: a step uses its agent's default runtime unless its required tools need another.
reworded.statement: While window steps are paused, runtime routing is suspended: a step would use its agent's default runtime unless its required tools need another.

reworded.topic: C-04 Window steps and the watcher
reworded.original: Suspended visibility: agent need, the Change's always-visible or the global switch makes a step a window chat with the same tools as unwatched; changes apply from the next session.
reworded.statement: While window steps are paused, visibility routing is suspended: agent need, Change always-visible or the global visibility switch makes a step a window chat with the same tools as unwatched; changes apply next session.
reworded.note: corrected by a second check: “Unwatched tools” is undefined and no longer clearly states equality with an unwatched step's tool list.

reworded.original: Who = agent file; how = skill; what this time = brief, plan, task; why = brief outcome and the owner's decisions; when and where = engine; tools = agent file plus tool schemas.
reworded.statement: Delivery responsibilities: who = agent file; how = skill; current work = brief, plan, task; why = brief outcome and owner decisions; when and where = engine; tools = agent file plus tool schemas.

reworded.original: Model = Settings; rules = agent boundaries and instructions; events = Delivery, not repository hooks; owner-invoked = prompt or user-invocable skill; done = criteria plus enforced result contract.
reworded.statement: Delivery responsibilities: model = Settings; rules = agent boundaries and instructions; events = Delivery, not repository hooks; owner invocation = prompt or user-invocable skill; done = criteria plus enforced result contract.

reworded.original: Substantial or shared procedures become skills; short single-role steps stay in the agent file; the engine keeps enforcement.
reworded.statement: Substantial or shared Delivery procedures become skills; short single-role steps stay in the agent file; Delivery's engine keeps enforcement.

reworded.original: Steps are strict: one agent, its own skills, project agents and skills off. In the owner's chat OwlBear limits only what it adds and hides its skill from the `/` menu.
reworded.statement: Delivery steps use one agent and its own skills, with project agents and skills off. In the owner's chat OwlBear limits only its additions and hides its shaping skill from the "/" menu.

reworded.original: SDK steps run with repository instructions on, its agents and skills off.
reworded.statement: SDK steps run with repository instructions on and repository agents and skills off.

reworded.original: On conflict Delivery's steps, tools and result format win; repository conventions and required checks still apply; real clashes ask the owner.
reworded.statement: On conflict with repository instructions, Delivery's steps, tools and result format win; repository conventions and required checks still apply; real clashes go to the owner.

reworded.original: "Project agents and skills off" in SDK steps is not built yet; until its fix after self-update step 5, steps may run with them discoverable.
reworded.statement: Disabling project agents and skills in SDK steps is not built yet; the fix follows idle automatic self-updates (self-update step 5). Until then, SDK steps may run with project agents and skills discoverable.

reworded.original: Approval is one list giving location, purpose, alternative and what declining means, approved per location and artifact kind; a new location or capability asks again.
reworded.statement: Approval of OwlBear installs outside repositories uses one list of location, purpose, alternative and consequences of declining, approved per location and artifact kind; a new location or capability asks again.

reworded.original: Only exceptions outside `~/.owlbear`: the `owlbear` link in `~/.local/bin`, login item in `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, `~/.copilot` shaper links; each asked for separately at install, removed by uninstall.
reworded.statement: OwlBear's only local-file exceptions outside ~/.owlbear are its command link in ~/.local/bin, login item in ~/Library/LaunchAgents and shaper links in ~/.copilot; each needs separate install consent and is removed by uninstall.

reworded.original: OwlBear's decision record, plan and build designs of unbuilt work stay in its repository, which GitHub's agents and reviewer read; they move once history.
reworded.statement: OwlBear's decision record, plan and unbuilt-work designs stay in OwlBear's repository for GitHub's agents and reviewer; move them to owlbear-data once they become history.

reworded.original: A project's folder name defaults to the repository name; Delivery asks the owner on a collision, and the name can be renamed later.
reworded.statement: A project's folder in owlbear-data defaults to its repository name; Delivery asks the owner on a collision, and the folder can be renamed later.

reworded.original: Machine-only: update channel and registered projects. Project-only: test preparations, data permissions and the PR marker.
reworded.statement: Delivery settings restricted to the machine are update channel and registered projects; settings restricted to a project are test preparations, data permissions and the PR attribution marker.

reworded.original: Session limits count agent sessions, never per model: machine-only (default 4) and per project, layered (default 2). Free slots go round-robin across projects, first-ready within one; waiting spends no budget.
reworded.statement: Agent-session limits, never per model: machine-only default 4; per-project default 2, layered built-in, global, machine, project. Free slots go round-robin by project, first-ready within each; waiting spends no budget.

reworded.original: Three tiers: dev (the Change's worktree), test, live; Delivery's checks never touch live.
reworded.statement: Delivery uses three tiers for checks: dev (the Change's worktree), test and live; Delivery's checks never touch live.

reworded.original: Test is a copy of live running the Change's code; one frozen snapshot is restored separately for the before and the after capture.
reworded.statement: Delivery's test tier is a copy of live running the Change's code; restore one frozen snapshot separately for the before and after screenshot captures.

reworded.original: The owner's standing per-project permissions cover data classes, keys, isolation and retention; with no safe option Delivery asks or blocks.
reworded.statement: The owner's standing per-project test-preparation permissions cover data classes, keys, isolation and retention; with no safe preparation option, Delivery asks or blocks.

reworded.original: Restore, seed, cleanup and checks get only declared variables; export and masking run only declared, committed scripts.
reworded.statement: For Delivery's test environments, restore, seed, cleanup and checks get only declared variables; export and masking run only declared, committed scripts.

reworded.original: Compare per Change, not per task. Retake "before" if the target's UI changed since shaping; the shaping set stays the design reference.
reworded.statement: Compare before and after screenshots per Change, not per task. Retake "before" if the target's UI changed since shaping; shaping screenshots remain the design reference.

reworded.original: The capture collects console errors, and page errors (uncaught exceptions) count as console errors: new ones since "before" fail the check, existing ones are reported.
reworded.statement: Screenshot capture collects console errors, including uncaught page exceptions: errors new since the "before" capture fail the visual check; existing errors are reported.

reworded.original: The detector's findings are evidence for the judges, never a fail on their own.
reworded.statement: The design detector's findings are evidence for the visual judges, never a visual-check failure on their own.

reworded.original: The owner passes or fails on one page with the comparison, both verdicts and findings. Fail needs a finding or comment, which becomes a next-review criterion, a Pass comment a note; brief contradictions are held.
reworded.statement: The owner decides on one visual-check page with screenshot comparison, both verdicts and findings. Fail needs a finding or comment; its comment becomes a next-review criterion. Pass comments stay notes; brief conflicts are held.
reworded.note: corrected by a second check: Makes selected findings, not only Fail comments, next-review criteria; TD-79 specifies the comment.

reworded.original: Three reviews: each task's build, the Change's end, the visual check; challenger and subagent judgements are not kept. The final review covers a task's last repair, CI and the PR the final loop's.
reworded.statement: Delivery reviews each task build, the whole Change and screenshots; challenger and subagent judgements are not kept. The final review covers a task's last repair; CI and the PR cover the final loop's last repair.

reworded.original: Build, final, plan, pack and brief loops have per-role settings: 3 rounds, 10 new findings per round, last round at 4 or fewer, owner at 7 or more.
reworded.statement: Delivery's build, final-review, plan, design-pack and brief loops have per-role settings: 3 rounds, 10 new findings per round, last round at 4 or fewer new findings, owner at 7 or more new findings at maximum rounds.

reworded.original: Repairs, progress and failures never reset a subject's round limit. From round 2, judge prior rejections and new findings, no other earlier ones; disputed rejections go to the owner before repair.
reworded.statement: Repairs, progress and failures never reset a review subject's round limit. From round 2, judge the previous round's rejections and new findings, no other earlier findings; disputed rejections go to the owner before repair.

reworded.original: A worker's reasoned rejection gets one independent fresh-session recheck, counted apart from repair rounds, before the owner is asked; if upheld, the owner is asked.
reworded.statement: A worker's reasoned rejection of a finding gets one independent fresh-session recheck, counted apart from repair rounds, before asking the owner; if the finding is upheld, ask the owner.

reworded.original: At or below the last-round threshold, end early. Every final round gets a rejections-only check outside the round count, with no new findings; disputed rejections go to the owner.
reworded.statement: A review or challenge loop ends early at or below its last-round finding threshold. Every loop's last round gets one rejections-only check outside the round count, with no new findings; disputed rejections go to the owner.

reworded.original: Repairs after the last round stay unreviewed and are shown with standing rejections. Only at max rounds with the owner threshold of new findings does he choose another round or reject and retry.
reworded.statement: After a review loop's last round, repairs stay unreviewed and are shown with standing rejections. Only at maximum rounds with the owner threshold of new findings does the owner choose another round or reject and retry.

reworded.original: The planner may reject plan-challenge findings with reasons, the same way as the builder and the pack updater.
reworded.statement: The planner may reject plan-challenge findings with reasons, under the builder and design-pack updater's rejection process: one independent fresh-session recheck, then ask the owner if the finding is upheld.

reworded.original: For an upheld rejection the owner chooses per finding Fix, Reconsider or Drop, never Pause; Reconsider needs a note and runs once per finding, outside rounds.
reworded.statement: When an independent recheck upholds a finding the worker rejected, the owner chooses Fix, Reconsider or Drop per finding, never Pause; Reconsider requires a note and runs once per finding, outside rounds.

reworded.original: A note contradicting the brief is held; Drop never waives a criterion and reopens only on new evidence; after Fix only a wrong premise may be raised.
reworded.statement: For disputed findings, owner notes contradicting the brief are held; Drop never waives a criterion, and a dropped finding reopens only on new evidence; after Fix, only a wrong premise may be raised.

reworded.original: Reconsidering may clarify or withdraw, never enlarge; an unsure finding returns once, then only Fix or Drop. Owner notes travel whole; owner-decided repairs commit; drops reach only outside reviews.
reworded.statement: Reconsidering a disputed finding may clarify or withdraw it, never enlarge it; unsure returns once, then only Fix or Drop. Owner notes travel whole; owner-decided repairs commit; drops reach only reviews outside the loop.

reworded.original: Added work is never reviewed twice: each later addition gets one final round beyond max, judging unjudged rejections, new commits in focus, not blind to the rest; task additions go to its next round.
reworded.statement: Never review added work twice: after final review ends, each addition gets one round beyond max, judging unjudged rejections and focusing on new commits without ignoring the rest; task additions go to that task's next round.

reworded.topic: C-13 Retry and Accept as done
reworded.original: Retry uses a fresh builder and the plan; final-review retry selects tasks or replans from the brief. Archive rejected attempts, never delete them.
reworded.statement: A task retry uses a fresh builder and the plan; a final-review retry selects tasks to rebuild or replans from the brief. Archive rejected attempts, never delete them.

reworded.topic: C-13 Retry and Accept as done
reworded.original: The owner selects tasks to rebuild; selecting none accepts the remaining findings as the owner's decision and continues to publishing.
reworded.statement: In a final-review retry, the owner selects tasks to rebuild; selecting none accepts the remaining findings as the owner's decision and continues to publishing.

reworded.topic: C-13 Retry and Accept as done
reworded.original: After a rebuild, the last rebuilt task's builder runs every kept task's checks and fixes failures, reviewed in its rounds; CI stays the second net.
reworded.statement: After a rebuild, the last rebuilt task's builder runs every kept task's checks and fixes failures; that rebuilt task's review rounds review the fixes, with CI as a second check.

reworded.original: Challenge the brief before approval; the shaper may revise or reject with reasons. Apply the shaper's round settings and show standing rejections at approval; no post-approval challenge.
reworded.statement: Challenge the brief before approval; the shaper may revise it or reject findings with reasons. Use the shaper's round settings and show standing rejections at approval; no post-approval brief challenge.

reworded.original: The shaper requests a challenge when the saved draft is ready.
reworded.statement: The shaper requests a brief challenge when the saved brief draft is ready.

reworded.original: Approval foregrounds outcome, owner decisions with origins, and non-goals; criteria, visual and person checks stay under collapsed technical details.
reworded.statement: Brief approval foregrounds outcome, owner decisions with origins, and non-goals; criteria, visual and person checks stay under collapsed technical details.

reworded.original: Levels follow origin, not field: the owner's direct choices are `decided`, generated items in the approval `approved`, later implementation choices `autonomous`; authorship and authority are recorded.
reworded.statement: Decision levels follow origin, not field: direct owner choices are decided, generated items included in brief approval are approved, later implementation choices are autonomous; authorship and authority are recorded.

reworded.original: Approve is a bounded delegation: the dialog says it authorises the work and intent-preserving changes, not new product commitments.
reworded.statement: Approving a brief is a bounded delegation: the approval dialog says it authorises the work and intent-preserving changes, not new product commitments.

reworded.original: Weaker means what could now pass that failed before, judged cumulatively.
reworded.statement: A brief amendment is weaker if it allows something to pass that previously failed; judge weakening cumulatively against the approved intent.

reworded.original: Only a redundant or over-specific generated check may be replaced, with independent evidence of equal coverage, else ask the owner; check tightening for scope, cost; never edit a check for a failing build.
reworded.statement: A brief amendment may replace only a redundant or over-specific generated check, with independent evidence of equal coverage; otherwise ask the owner. Check tightening for scope and cost; never change a check because a build fails.

reworded.original: Anyone proposes, the artifact's owner prepares, an independent challenger judges the exact change; doubt about intent goes to the owner. Existing loops and limits apply, changes batched per challenge.
reworded.statement: Anyone may propose a brief amendment; the artifact's owner prepares it and an independent challenger judges the exact change. Intent doubts go to the owner; Delivery's review loops and limits apply, changes batched per challenge.

reworded.original: Scope of amendments: criteria, UI flag, visual states, person checks, constraints, assumptions; plan tasks and test commands stay autonomous.
reworded.statement: Brief amendments cover criteria, UI flag, visual states, person checks, constraints and assumptions; plan tasks and test commands stay autonomous.

reworded.original: The approved baseline is kept; every later change is listed (old → new, reason, level, challenger); an objection pauses dependent work; undo is promised only where possible.
reworded.statement: Keep the approved brief baseline; list every later amendment with old and new values, reason, level and challenger. An objection pauses dependent work; promise undo only where possible.

reworded.original: Design amendments end to end before adding amendment code; until then proposals may be challenged and recorded but must not be applied.
reworded.statement: Design the brief-amendment process end to end before adding amendment code; until then, amendment proposals may be challenged and recorded but must not be applied.

reworded.original: Settings offers one update for detector and skills together, with affected checks and an independent challenge of the whole pack.
reworded.statement: Settings offers one design-pack update for detector and skills together, with affected checks and an independent challenge of the whole design pack.

reworded.original: The updater may change its whole candidate, but only in its own folder and without shell access; read upstream skills at the pinned revision.
reworded.statement: The design-pack updater may change its whole candidate, but only in its own folder and without shell access; read upstream skills at the pinned revision.

reworded.original: A change to the detector's or adapter's code is checked with the running code; the owner approves its diff and CI's unit tests must pass.
reworded.statement: When a design-pack update changes detector or adapter code, checks use the running code; the owner approves the diff and CI's unit tests must pass.

reworded.original: Affected checks rerun after its edits; changing expected evidence (golden expectations, calibration) asks the owner.
reworded.statement: Rerun affected checks after the design-pack updater's edits; changing expected evidence, including golden expectations and calibration, asks the owner.

reworded.original: The challenger checks each change is needed by the upgrade and asks the owner when unsure, with every changed file and one line per file on what changed and why it is suspicious.
reworded.statement: The design-pack challenger checks each change is needed by the upgrade and asks the owner when unsure, listing every changed file with one line per file on what changed and why it is suspicious.

reworded.original: Its challenge rounds follow C-12's loop with the updater's values.
reworded.statement: Design-pack update challenges follow Delivery's review-and-challenge loop rules, using the design-pack updater's settings.

reworded.original: Without a pass, stop before activating and ask: activate the unreviewed repair or discard. Another round only at max rounds with the owner threshold of findings; Discard whenever waiting.
reworded.statement: If a design-pack challenge ends without a pass, stop before activation and ask: activate the unreviewed repair or discard. Offer another round only at max rounds with the owner finding threshold; offer Discard whenever waiting.

reworded.original: Every pack update opens a PR; its merge activates it as machines take the version. The challenger's pass, owner approval of detector code changes and his word on an unreviewed repair gate it.
reworded.statement: Every design-pack update opens a PR; its merge activates the pack as machines take the version. The challenger's pass, owner approval of detector code changes and the owner's word on an unreviewed repair gate the PR.

reworded.original: Its PR gets OwlBear's PR labels and becomes a version as they say.
reworded.statement: A design-pack update's PR gets the labels OwlBear adds to every PR it opens and becomes a version according to its release labels.

reworded.original: A workflow makes the tag once that merge commit's own CI passes.
reworded.statement: OwlBear's release workflow creates a version tag after a labelled PR merges to main and that merge commit's own CI passes.

reworded.original: Tags are created with a fine-grained token the owner makes (this repository; Contents and Workflows write) and stores as the Actions secret `RELEASE_TOKEN`; it serves only that.
reworded.statement: OwlBear version tags use an owner-created fine-grained token for maba-pag/owlbear, with Contents and Workflows write, stored as the Actions secret RELEASE_TOKEN and used only to create tags.

reworded.original: No label is checked or protected; no CI check asks for or checks a label.
reworded.statement: No OwlBear PR label is checked or protected; no CI check asks for or checks a label.

reworded.original: A design pack update's pull request gets those labels and becomes a version as they say.
reworded.statement: A design-pack update's PR gets the labels OwlBear adds to every PR it opens and becomes a version according to its release labels.

reworded.original: Never track `main`. Automatically take the newest version in the machine's chosen channel: every minor by default, or majors only.
reworded.statement: OwlBear's installed runtime never tracks main; it automatically takes the newest version in the machine's chosen channel: every minor by default, or majors only.

reworded.original: The runtime never moves backwards on its own.
reworded.statement: The installed OwlBear runtime never moves backwards on its own.

reworded.original: Update when idle and Update while paused start on; automatic updates obey both; Run updates now still works, as does an owner's pack update started while paused.
reworded.statement: OwlBear's Update when idle and Update while paused settings start on; automatic updates obey both. Run updates now and an owner's design-pack update started while paused still work.

reworded.original: After each merge, Run updates now (`owlbear update`) takes the tagged version; a failed update is repaired forward by hand (recommendation taken once step 4 was built and rehearsed).
reworded.statement: After each merge, Run updates now (owlbear update) takes the tagged version; repair failed updates forward by hand, as adopted after version installation and handover were built and rehearsed.

reworded.original: Login and post-crash starts are paused; a start from stopped runs; restarts and updates keep their running or paused state; a paused start on purpose remains possible.
reworded.statement: OwlBear login and post-crash starts are paused; a start from stopped runs; restarts and updates keep their running or paused state; a paused start on purpose remains possible.

reworded.original: The pause holds Delivery's automatic work on Changes; the owner's own actions and the listed maintenance run.
reworded.statement: Delivery's pause holds automatic work on Changes; the owner's own actions and maintenance, including design-pack updates, self-updates and cleanup, run.

reworded.original: Answers and approvals take effect and show as answered immediately; resulting automatic Change work waits for Resume.
reworded.statement: While Delivery is paused, answers and approvals take effect and show as answered immediately; resulting automatic Change work waits for Resume.

reworded.original: Paused pages offer Resume and Run updates now; updates also run pending maintenance but wait for pre-pause steps, with the reason shown.
reworded.statement: Paused Delivery pages offer Resume and Run updates now; Run updates now also runs pending maintenance but waits for steps running before the pause, with the reason shown.

reworded.original: Add project offers an existing folder or a new project; the installer may open it at its end.
reworded.statement: Delivery's Add project offers an existing folder or a new project; the installer may open the Add project choice when installation ends.

reworded.original: A project created this way is a real project: Delivery's work on it waits for the watcher.
reworded.statement: A project created through Delivery's new-project flow is a real project: Delivery's work on it waits for the watcher.

reworded.original: The machine host's web UI is the one UI (TD-85's "cockpit" meant it); the old Cockpit was audited, its memory purge ported and Cockpit deleted before v1.0.
reworded.statement: Delivery's machine-host web UI is its only UI; TD-85's "cockpit" meant that UI. The old Cockpit was audited, its memory purge ported, and Cockpit deleted before v1.0.
reworded.note: corrected by a second check: Generalises the clarification of TD-85's “cockpit” to every earlier cockpit request.

reworded.original: TD-85's module tabs are done; its end-to-end review of the pages' user flows and information and their visual overhaul are one backlog entry.
reworded.statement: Delivery's module tabs are done; the end-to-end review of its web pages' user flows and information and their visual overhaul form one backlog entry.

reworded.original: CodeRabbit reviews quietly as `.coderabbit.yaml` sets, the review brief its guideline, early access off.
reworded.statement: CodeRabbit reviews quietly according to its repository configuration, using OwlBear's code-review instructions as its guideline; early access stays off.

reworded.original: Agents label a PR that changes runtime code or CI workflows once its CI passed and merge it only after the review is in and handled, or after 60 minutes without one, said in the PR; others merge after CI and Sol's review.
reworded.statement: After CI passes, agents add coderabbit to runtime-code or CI-workflow PRs; merge after CodeRabbit review is handled, or after 60 minutes without one, noted in the PR. Other PRs merge after CI and Sol review.

reworded.original: `h-decision-requests`, `h-process-observations` and `w-deviation-audit` retire with batch 3, once checked that the new engine holds what they offer.
reworded.statement: Retire h-decision-requests, h-process-observations and w-deviation-audit with batch 3 of old Delivery's removal, after checking the new engine holds what those skills offer.

reworded.original: Group files by responsibility or kind, named for their readers; keep role agents and skills top-level, without a content umbrella.
reworded.statement: Group Delivery package files by responsibility or kind, named for their readers; keep role agents and skills at the package root, without a content umbrella.

reworded.original: Each package folder holds one responsibility and imports only folders before it in the layer order; a test enforces it.
reworded.statement: Each folder in Delivery's Python package holds one responsibility and imports only folders earlier in the package's dependency-layer order; a test enforces that order.

reworded.original: Use Cyclopts: instant completion without starting Python, no shell startup-file edits, and lazy commands.
reworded.statement: The owlbear command uses Cyclopts: instant completion without starting Python, no shell startup-file edits, and lazy commands.

reworded.original: Ask about starting at login once at install; allow later CLI opt-in/out and show it in the CLI and settings. If macOS blocks it, say so and keep on-demand use.
reworded.statement: Ask once at installation whether OwlBear should start at login; allow later CLI opt-in or opt-out and show the setting in CLI and Settings. If macOS blocks login startup, report it and keep on-demand use.

reworded.original: Collect potential changes in an evidence-linked inbox; the owner classifies them, adds context, connects several and creates linked Changes.
reworded.statement: Collect potential changes in an evidence-linked backlog inbox; the owner classifies them, adds context, connects several and creates linked Changes.

reworded.original: Repeats are counted in a summary in the issue, comments only for new evidence.
reworded.statement: Count repeated backlog reports in a summary in their GitHub issue; use comments only for new evidence.

reworded.original: Entries may name several projects or none. Repeats merge only when they name the same projects (or both none); otherwise they are linked.
reworded.statement: Backlog entries may name several projects or none. Repeated reports merge only when they name the same projects, or both name none; otherwise link the entries.

reworded.original: A finding names the project it was found in, none outside any; an untriaged entry names its origin; they merge only on equal sets.
reworded.statement: A backlog finding names the project where it was found, or none outside any project; an untriaged entry names its origin project. Merge backlog entries only when their project sets match.

reworded.original: A repeat that does not merge is linked to every matching entry at once; the owner can unlink it.
reworded.statement: Link a repeated backlog report that does not merge to every matching backlog entry immediately; the owner can unlink it.

reworded.original: Project-specific lessons stay in the project; general ones go to Global. The saving agent recommends the scope; the entry waits unused in its project until curated.
reworded.statement: Project-specific memory lessons stay in the project; general lessons go to Global. The saving agent recommends the scope; the memory entry waits unused in its project until curated.

reworded.original: Above one Global confidence threshold (95% at first) the curator decides alone, Make global included; below it, it asks (interactive mode) or skips (automatic mode); interactive sessions propose Make global.
reworded.statement: Above one Global confidence threshold, initially 95%, the memory curator decides alone, including Make global; below it, ask in interactive mode or skip in automatic mode. Interactive sessions propose Make global.

reworded.original: Reviewers run in parallel as Delivery steps of their own, each with its role's values, credits and retry; the curator step then checks their verdicts.
reworded.statement: Test reviewers run in parallel as separate Delivery steps, each with its role's settings, credits and retry; the test-curator step then checks their verdicts.

reworded.original: Reviewers default to Sol, medium effort, default context; the curator to Opus 5.5, high effort, long context; both are roles in Settings.
reworded.statement: Test reviewers default to Sol, medium effort, default context; the test curator defaults to Opus 5.5, high effort, long context; both are roles in Settings.

reworded.original: Keep, rewrite lower, merge or retire; doubt keeps. A removal names the behaviour, a plausible bug and the test that still catches it; security guards, incident regressions and public contracts stay.
reworded.statement: In test curation, keep, rewrite at a lower layer, merge or retire; doubt keeps. Each removal names the behaviour, a plausible bug and the surviving test catching it; security guards, incident regressions and public contracts stay.

reworded.original: Later, the watcher infers the stages inside an agent session (preparation, working, challenge and fixing rounds, finalizing), which may differ by role.
reworded.statement: Once built, the watcher infers stages inside agent sessions: preparation, working, challenge and fixing rounds, finalizing; stages may differ by role.

reworded.original: Step kinds are a guide, not a gate: a new kind is allowed when no existing step can run its work, recorded with its reason; above eleven (the design's ten and the test review's) the count is reported, not failed.
reworded.statement: Delivery step kinds are a guide, not a gate: a new kind is allowed when no existing step can do its work; record why. Above eleven (the design's ten plus test review), report the count, never fail it.
reworded.note: corrected by a second check: Adds “only”: permission when existing kinds cannot do the work becomes an exclusive prohibition in other circumstances.

reworded.original: They also say the way forward if he declines, with cost and disruption where they apply; buttons name the action.
reworded.statement: Confirmations for consequential buttons also explain the way forward if the owner declines, with cost and disruption where applicable; buttons name the action.

reworded.original: Pass confirms only at the last gate before an automatic merge. Fail always confirms and needs a note, used as written for the fix unless it contradicts the approved brief; then it is held for the owner.
reworded.statement: For person checks, Pass confirms only at the last gate before automatic merge. Fail always confirms and needs a note, used as written for the fix unless it contradicts the approved brief; then hold it for the owner.

reworded.original: Use shows per role on the Maintenance page; a Settings switch per role, on by default, turns subagents on or off.
reworded.statement: Subagent use appears per role on Maintenance; a per-role Settings switch, on by default, turns subagents on or off.

reworded.original: Charter parts no later decision replaced keep their `approved` origin from the charter and design approval; §3.8's allow list was replaced.
reworded.statement: Unreplaced parts of the Delivery-next charter keep their approved origin from charter and design approval; the charter's default-deny permission allow list was replaced.

reworded.original: The pages load the Porsche Design System only from its documented CDN: no own fallback rendering or load diagnostic; browser tests reach the real CDN.
reworded.statement: Delivery's web pages load the Porsche Design System only from its documented CDN: no own fallback rendering or load diagnostic; browser tests reach the real CDN.

reworded.original: On those pages dialogs close with PDS's dismiss button and Escape and the confirmation does not focus Cancel first; screenshot thumbnails stay plain image buttons, as PDS has no image button.
reworded.statement: Delivery web dialogs close with Porsche Design System's dismiss button and Escape; confirmations do not focus Cancel first. Screenshot thumbnails stay plain image buttons because that design system has no image button.

reworded.original: Fixing memory publication and curation (F17) follows the plan's order; M4 and M5 no longer exist.
reworded.statement: Fixing memory publication and curation follows the OwlBear plan's work order; the old build and first-real-project milestones, M4 and M5, no longer exist.

reworded.original: In-force lines state intent in at most two lines each; how something is built lives in code, tests and pull request texts, not here.
reworded.statement: In-force statements in OwlBear's decision record state intent in at most two lines each; implementation belongs in code, tests and PR texts, not the decision record.

reworded.original: A decision records only the owner's confirmed intent; his words are never stored, in decision files, this record or commit messages; the record's existing quotes stay as history until the migration.
reworded.statement: Record only confirmed owner intent, never the owner's words, in decision files, OwlBear's decision record or commit messages; existing quotes in the decision record stay as history until its migration.

reworded.original: A read-only owlbear-data token serves only a workflow on pushes to main and a daily schedule; pull-request CI checks the generated view's own hash.
reworded.statement: A read-only owlbear-data token serves only OwlBear's decision-view generation workflow on pushes to main and a daily schedule; PR CI checks the generated decision view's own hash.

reworded.original: Today's rules come over as inherited: their recorded authority, marked never read back, without quotes; one is read back only when work relies on it and its meaning is unclear.
reworded.statement: The decision-record migration inherits existing rules with their recorded authority, marked never read back and without quotes; read one back only when work relies on it and its meaning is unclear.

reworded.original: Global: C-01's asking rules (not page comments), security changes reviewed with the owner, consumer research out of its project, config changes the owner approves, the nine ECC adoptions; all else is OwlBear's.
reworded.statement: Global: C-01's asking rules except page comments; owner review of security changes; consumer research kept out of its project; owner-approved lint/format configs, CI workflows and Git hooks; nine ECC adoptions. All else is OwlBear's.
reworded.note: corrected by a second check: Broadens consumer-project research exclusion to research generally; drops formatter configurations from the approval list.

reworded.original: Within approved work or a delegation agents decide reversible details and record consequential ones as theirs; anything lasting, wider, contrary to an owner decision or committing outside asks first.
reworded.statement: Within approved or delegated work, agents choose reversible details and record consequential ones as theirs; anything lasting, wider, contrary to an owner decision or externally committing (cost, accounts, publishing) asks the owner first.
reworded.note: corrected by a second check: “Committing outside” remains ambiguous: outside a worktree, outside the delegation, or an external commitment. The build document identifies cost, accounts and publishing.

reworded.original: Workers get the decisions assigned to their work and may look up more in Global and their project; challengers check the complete list.
reworded.statement: Change workers get their assigned decisions and may look up more Global and project decisions; challengers check the complete Global and project decision list.

reworded.original: Shaping decisions apply from brief approval, project-wide ones to the project's other Changes at once; chat and page decisions apply at confirmation.
reworded.statement: Decisions made in shaping apply at brief approval; project-wide ones then apply to the project's other Changes immediately. Decisions made in chat or on a page apply at confirmation.
reworded.note: corrected by a second check: Narrows “page decisions” to the Decisions page, excluding decisions confirmed through other pages, including Change clarifications.

reworded.original: A failed lookup shows as failed, never as "no rules apply"; no fixed size limit; a short log of wrong picks and misses, each with the condition that made it wrong, corrects the picker; no statistics or automatic filters.
reworded.statement: Failed decision lookups show failure, never "no rules apply"; decision sets have no fixed size limit. A short log of wrong picks and misses, each with the condition making it wrong, corrects the picker; no statistics or automatic filters.

reworded.original: A separate picker on Sol at medium effort picks a Change's rules at shaping and answers every later lookup of workers and lead chats, reading the complete list.
reworded.statement: A separate decision picker on Sol at medium effort picks a Change's rules at shaping and answers every later worker or lead-chat lookup by reading the complete Global and project decision list.

reworded.original: Every worker of a Change gets the whole picked set; no agent trims it.
reworded.statement: Every Change worker gets the whole decision set picked for that Change; no agent trims it.

reworded.original: Rules carry no role or kind tags and there are no per-role views.
reworded.statement: Decision rules carry no role or kind tags and have no per-role views.

reworded.original: An answer during the work is classified by its relayer as event, clarification or brief change; clarifications are read back and become Change decisions; a Sol check stops the work when one changes the brief.
reworded.statement: An answer during a Change is classified by its relayer as event, clarification or brief change; clarifications are read back and become Change decisions; a Sol check stops work when a clarification changes the brief.
